Hi all — quick summary and what we can provide. I tried to keep this auditor-friendly and short.

1) Tenant-scoped retention enforcement (how we do it)- We use per-tenant metadata tags at write-time; retention policies are enforced by the data-lifecycle service which deletes data after TTL expiration. For inference telemetry we keep two logical categories: "debug traces" (user-facing debug payloads, default 90d for Medispec per request) and "aggregated telemetry" (rollups/metrics, default 7d).

2) Evidence types we can deliver- Proof-of-delete manifest: a CSV listing object ids, hash (SHA256), deletion timestamp, and deletion job run-id.
- Keystore access sample: we can include a 7-day slice of keystore access logs showing the key rotation and usage (PII identifiers redacted).
- API invocation traces: we can produce an audit log snippet showing the delegated deletion API call, including HMAC signature verification and server-evaluated result (success/failure).
- Snapshot of retention policy config as of deletion time (JSON export).

3) Delegated deletion options- Option A (recommended): customer-managed service account that signs deletion requests using a scoped HMAC key. Redwood validates signature and records the invocation in the audit-trail; deletion then runs as a scheduled job for that tenant with run-id tied to the signed request.
- Option B: Redwood-initiated deletion on behalf of the customer after an authenticated request via our secure portal (less operational burden for customer).

4) CAIQ / SIG mapping (high level)- CAIQ: CCM 10 (Data Retention & Erasure) — we will mark the provided artifacts that map to CCM10.
- SIG: evidence for "Data Retention" control family: manifest, keystore logs, and audit traces satisfy SIG requests for proof of erasure and key control. If the auditor demands, we can provide a redacted sample pack tied to a real deletion job id.

5) Multi-party proof considerations- For higher assurance, we can produce a hash-chain manifest: store the manifest hash in our immutable ledger and provide the ledger receipt as part of the packet. That provides tamper-evidence without notarization.

6) Timeline and deliverables- If Medispec returns the completed form today, we can: draft packet (June 4), finalize artifact hand-off (June 7) including Drive folder + manifest + 2 example logs. If they need DocuSign notarization of a deletion certificate, add 3 business days.

Attached I dropped a small CSV template (evidence_manifest.csv) and a redacted keystore access sample (keystore_access_log_sample.txt) for illustration.

Kimberly Park
